newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece seeks 3-month delay in EU diesel law - PPC.
newsitem.headline: Greece seeks 3-month delay in EU diesel law - PPC.

text.p: Greece's development ministry has requested an extension of the October 1 EU deadline for low sulphur diesel to January 1, Public Petroleum Corp (PPC) managing director Lazaros Lazaridis told Reuters on Friday.
New European anti-pollution laws require EU states to introduce lower sulphur diesel at their pumps by October 1, but Greece and Portugal have asked for an extension of the deadline.
Lazaridis said he was not sure of the official response from Brussels to the request but said official procedures had been followed.
He told Reuters that Greece was not trying to get a waiver from the EU on the law, but PPC simply needed more time to exhaust the higher sulphur diesel in its tanks.

He said PPC will start production of the new 0.05 percent sulphur diesel on October 1, but still had oil storage tanks containing 0.2 percent sulphur diesel and it would take three months to use it up.
Lazaridis said, however, that sulphur content would gradually be coming down during this period and come January 1 only 0.05 sulphur diesel would be available.
